Optimal.Notes: Setting the refresh rate to 40 Hz and capping frames to match gives a smooth, tear-free experience at modest power draw. UI Scale should be increased from the default for comfortable readability on the 7-inch screen.

profiles.Summary: RimWorld is a lightweight 2D colony sim that runs excellently on the Steam Deck, well within the hardware's capabilities even in late-game large colonies. The game is Steam Deck Verified with partial controller support, though mouse-and-keyboard style input via touchscreen or trackpad is often preferred for complex colony management.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's lightweight 2D nature, minimal PC requirements (Intel HD 4000 GPU), and the Deck's hardware capabilities. On your first run, check the UI Scale setting for readability and monitor frame rate during a large raid to confirm the CPU is not the bottleneck in your colony size.

MaxBattery.Notes: RimWorld is CPU/logic-bound rather than GPU-bound, so a very low TDP and GPU clock are sufficient. A 30 fps cap with a 4 W TDP limit maximises session length without impacting gameplay feel in this turn-paced sim.

KnownIssues: UI text and menus can be very small at native 1280x800; use the in-game UI scale setting to increase readability.
Partial controller support means some actions are easier with the trackpad or touchscreen than with thumbsticks.
Very late-game large colonies with many pawns and events can cause occasional CPU-bound slowdowns.
Mods from Steam Workshop may require additional Proton compatibility tweaks or cause instability.

MaxPerformance.Notes: RimWorld is not GPU-limited, so automatic GPU clocks are fine; the bottleneck in large colonies is CPU simulation speed. 60 fps is easily achievable in early-to-mid game, though very large late-game colonies may dip to 45–55 fps during raids.

Optimal.Notes: 60 fps at a modest 7 W TDP gives a smooth, comfortable experience for most colony sizes; UI Scale at 150% makes menus readable on the small screen. Late-game mega-colonies may dip slightly but remain very playable.

profiles.Summary: RimWorld is a lightweight 2D/top-down indie colony sim with very modest GPU demands, well within the Steam Deck's capabilities, and runs natively well under Proton with a Verified rating. The game is CPU-bound during large late-game colonies, but even then the Deck handles it comfortably at 60 fps with a low TDP.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very low PC minimum requirements (Intel HD 4000, Core 2 Duo) and its 2D/top-down rendering nature. On your first run, check the frame counter during a mid-game colony event — if it holds 60 fps easily, the Optimal profile is conservative and you can try MaxPerformance; if a late-game colony causes dips, reduce the game speed setting in-game rather than adjusting graphics.

MaxBattery.Notes: RimWorld's GPU load is minimal; the TDP and GPU clock are set very low since the bottleneck is CPU simulation. A 30 fps cap at 4 W TDP maximises battery life while keeping the game fully playable.

KnownIssues: UI text and menus may be small at 1280x800; use the in-game UI scale slider to compensate.
Late-game large colonies with many pawns and events can cause CPU-side frame dips.
Partial controller support means some actions are easier with the touchscreen or trackpad than face buttons.
Mods from Steam Workshop may require additional Proton compatibility tweaks or cause instability.

MaxPerformance.Notes: RimWorld is not GPU-limited so uncapping the frame rate and pushing all visual settings to maximum is safe; the game will sit at or near 90 fps in early/mid colonies. The real ceiling is the CPU simulation tick speed in very large late-game colonies, not the GPU.
